dedupe_keys.name: volcanic hazard assessment map for the reykjanes eruptions icelandic meteorological office

description: The Icelandic Meteorological Office publishes a hazard assessment map for the volcanic systems on the Reykjanes peninsula. The version read is valid from 30 June 2026 and will next be updated on 30 September unless changes in activity call for a new version. The map has three parts: the alert level of the volcanic system on a four-step scale from 0 (green) to 3 (red) under the new volcano alert level system (VALS); mapped hazards, combining seven hazard factors for the Svartsengi system (seismic activity, collapse into fissures, fissure movement, vent opening, lava flow, tephra fall and gas pollution) into a cumulative hazard level assessed per pixel down to 20 metres and shown on a six-step colour scale; and selected observation areas, for which the average hazard level is computed and the hazards rated high or very high are listed. The page explains the data used for each hazard, including monitoring data, model results, forecasts and expert judgement. Access is free online; no licence is stated on the page read. Caveats: uncoloured areas are rated very low but hazard cannot be ruled out there, the map changes with activity, and the page is in Icelandic. Coverage is the Reykjanes peninsula. It supports hazard exposure analysis of roads, power lines, pipelines and the town of Grindavík; related records are the Reykjanes hazard and risk reports and the IG-EPN seismic and volcanic data.
